en.title: Kojima Details Sony's PHYSINT Cancellation and Dramatic Xbox Pivot
en.summary: Hideo Kojima breaks his silence on Sony's abrupt cancellation of the ambitious action-espionage game PHYSINT. The legendary developer reveals the stunning news and the subsequent high-stakes scramble to find a new home for the project.
en.body:
In a candid conversation, legendary game designer **Hideo Kojima** has shed light on the unexpected decision by **Sony PlayStation** to pull the plug on his highly anticipated action-espionage title, **PHYSINT**. The move, which left Kojima and his studio, **Kojima Productions**, in a precarious position, has now led to a dramatic partnership with **Xbox**.

Kojima recounted the moment he received the news in June, during a Zoom call with Sony representatives. He was simultaneously working on **Xbox**'s **OD** and **PHYSINT**, the latter conceived as a spiritual successor to the iconic **Metal Gear Solid** series. The abrupt cancellation of **PHYSINT** sent shockwaves through **Kojima Productions**, forcing the developer to confront the potential collapse of his company. He expressed immediate concerns about the future of his staff, particularly those dedicated to **PHYSINT**, and how the decision would impact financial commitments, including loans secured after the release of **Death Stranding**.

> "I was so stunned by what Sony told me that my mind went blank." — Hideo Kojima

The situation evoked painful memories of the **P.T.** cancellation, a period that also caused significant upheaval for **Kojima Productions**. Faced with this setback, Kojima and his team spent three months tirelessly seeking a new partner to bring **PHYSINT** to life. This period involved extensive negotiations and advice-seeking across various industry sectors.

## A New Vision with Xbox

The search culminated in an agreement with **Xbox**, a partnership **Kojima** described as being built on a shared vision for the future. This marks a significant shift, as **PHYSINT**, previously a PlayStation exclusive, may now launch on a different platform entirely. **Kojima** emphasized his determination to keep the project alive, highlighting **Xbox**'s swift action in securing the game.

> "In the course of seeking advice and pursuing negotiations with people across many fields, we found in XBOX a partner with whom we share a common vision for the future, and we have decided to team up with them once again." — Hideo Kojima

This collaboration with **Xbox** underscores **Kojima**'s commitment to his creative endeavors, even when faced with major publisher hurdles. The decision to move **PHYSINT** to **Xbox** is a testament to the game's potential and **Kojima**'s enduring influence in the industry.

## Fan Reactions and Future Implications

The news has ignited significant discussion among gamers, many of whom view **PlayStation**'s decision as a major misstep. The abrupt cancellation of a project helmed by a developer of **Kojima**'s caliber, especially one with ties to the beloved **Metal Gear Solid** legacy, has left many fans disappointed and questioning **Sony**'s strategy. The move to **Xbox** has, however, generated considerable excitement among **Xbox** players who are eager to see **Kojima**'s latest creation.

## What's Next

Development of **PHYSINT** is ongoing under **Kojima Productions** with **Xbox**'s support. Specific release windows or further platform details have not yet been announced, but the project is confirmed to be moving forward.

content_raw: In June, Sony asked Hideo Kojima to attend a Zoom call. At the time, he was busy working on Xbox game OD and PlayStation game Physint , the latter a spiritual successor to the video game series that made him one of the most celebrated developers on the planet: Metal Gear Solid. For the meeting, he brought along Kojima Productions president Shinji Hirano and head of talent development Aki Saito. Kojima tells IGN in his first interview since last week’s dramatic news that he was so stunned by what Sony told him that his mind went blank. PlayStation was pulling out of the Physint project, and funding for it would end. And that was that. Kojima initially kept the news from his staff at Kojima Productions as he worried over the future of his company. Would he have to let developers from the Physint team go? Would they leave anyway, given what had happened? What would the bank, whose loans helped Kojima Productions staff up after the release of Death Stranding, think? And what about all the actors he’d already scanned for Physint? Was this a P.T. situation all over again? As we know, Kojima convinced Microsoft and new Xbox boss Asha Sharma to pick up Physint in one of the most dramatic console switches in history. Now the previous PlayStation exclusive may not release on PlayStation at all. In our interview, Kojima tells IGN Japan’s Daniel Robson how he feared Kojima Productions might collapse as a result of Sony's decision, and details his game-saving pitch to Xbox, which was quick to snap Physint up. It’s important to note that the interview was conducted before Bloomberg’s report that Sony ditched Physint due to missed deadlines, budget concerns, and Death Stranding’s alleged commercial failings . Kojima Productions provided a statement to IGN, which appears at the end of this interview, following a request for comment. In it, Kojima Productions insists the studio is "in a healthy, profitable state, development for Physint continues to move forward with Xbox, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong.​" Hideo Kojima: We are an independent company, so no funding is behind us as a corporation. We sign contracts according to projects, and that's how we survive one by one as an indie. So I need to find a new project before the previous project ends, and that's how we stay alive. Anyway, I know there's a lot of news in the game industry that many studios are closing down, many titles are canceled, and I understand the situation in the industry as a whole. But I thought Physint was okay. That Physint was safe. So I was surprised. But not just surprised. We didn’t understand the reason.
